exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean delivery vs. vaginal delivery)
Timing of cesarean delivery (antepartum non-indicated vs. intrapartum indicated)
outcome: Combined severe maternal outcomes (maternal death, transfusion, or hysterectomy)
cohort: 108,847 women who delivered in 39 hospitals across 14 provinces in China in 2011
finding: In 2011, when 81% of deliveries were among women having their first child, antepartum non-indicated cesarean delivery had similar short-term maternal and perinatal outcomes compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Compared to vaginal delivery, antepartum non-indicated cesarean delivery was associated with a decreased likelihood of postpartum hemorrhage and was not associated with increased risk of other adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes; however, intrapartum indicated cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage.
